title: Beyond the rainbow
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Visible light is only one part of the electromagnetic spectrum. Telescopes can be designed to detect infrared, radio, X-ray and other wavelengths that our eyes cannot see.

misconception: A learner may choose: Only visible green light
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: Which radiation can a telescope detect even though it is outside ordinary human vision?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: Which radiation can a telescope detect even though it is outside ordinary human vision? Infrared light. Visible light is only one part of the electromagnetic spectrum. Telescopes can be designed to detect infrared, radio, X-ray and other wavelengths that our eyes cannot see.
Visual caption: Visible is one small band. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.
